title: Milan: incline intervals are back on, 5 x 5min at 10-12%
terrain: treadmill 10-12% incline, climbing only, zero descent
coachNotes: PHYSIO VERDICT, 26 AUGUST, THIS SUPERSEDES THE 24 AUGUST SUSPENSION. Minor inflammation confirmed at the RIGHT lateral knee, left side clean. Shockwave delivered, energy 17 total each side. Agreed with the physio: training continues including intensity, the shockwave is there to speed recovery and not to replace load management; today 26 August is off; from 27 August training resumes; a second shockwave session next week if pain returns; the race is a GO. This is better information than any of the gates I wrote on 24 August, so those gates are retired and replaced by what follows. RESTORED FROM 5x4min BACK TO 5x5min, LOAD 75 -> 80. The 24 August cut existed because the week had lost its justification for a hard day and I could not tell what the band was doing. Both of those are now answered: a clinician has hands-on confirmation that this is minor and localised, and has cleared intensity explicitly. The session is still run UPHILL and not on the flat, and that is deliberate rather than residual caution. ITBS is a compression syndrome provoked by the knee cycling repeatedly through roughly 20-30 degrees of flexion under load, which is what flat and especially downhill running deliver. Steep uphill running keeps the knee largely outside that band and has no eccentric braking phase, so it buys you the exact quality Pirin asks for, 1900m of continuous ascent off the gun, at close to zero cost to the band. With 17 days left there is no reason to take intensity anywhere else. THE ONE THING TO BE CAREFUL ABOUT, AND IT IS NOT THE INFLAMMATION. Shockwave has a real short-term analgesic effect, typically over the first few days, and it works by desensitising the treated tissue. That means for roughly the next 3-5 days 'it does not hurt' is a weaker piece of evidence than it was last week: your main monitoring instrument has been partially switched off. So this week you follow the written session and stop where the plan says stop, rather than extending because the knee feels quiet. Symptoms are still worth reporting, a symptom now counts double, but their absence does not buy you extra volume until roughly Sunday. TODAY IS ROUGHLY 24 HOURS POST-SHOCKWAVE. Shockwave works by provoking a controlled inflammatory healing response, so the treated tissue is deliberately irritated right now and is normally kept off maximal direct loading for 24-48 hours. Uphill treadmill is the right compromise: high cardiovascular intensity, minimal mechanical demand on the lateral knee. Expect the site to feel bruised or tender to touch today, that is the treatment and not a relapse. What would be a relapse is pain that appears DURING running and worsens with duration. EXECUTION: hold the gradient fixed at 10-12% and drop the belt speed if HR runs over 94%. Never shorten the reps to hold pace, the gradient is the point. Walk the belt if that is what 12% demands, power-hiking steep ground is a Pirin skill and it trains the same system. Rep five should look like rep one. Two minutes flat walking between reps, do not jog them. OPTIMAL LOAD RULE, THE GOVERNING GATE: a session passes only if it produces no symptoms during it, none immediately after, and none the next day. Any one of the three is a fail, and the next session drops back to the last level that passed. The ceiling during a run is 2/10 with no spike afterwards; mild is allowed, new or worsening is not. HIP BLOCK AFTER, and it is the actual ITBS intervention: side-lying hip abduction 3x15 per side, clamshells 3x15 per side, single-leg glute bridges 3x12 per side, side plank with top-leg abduction 3x30s per side, Copenhagen planks 3x20s per side, single-leg calf raises 3x15. Hip abductor weakness with contralateral pelvic drop is the mechanism that lets the band compress the lateral epicondyle. STEP-DOWNS, SPLIT SQUATS AND LUNGES STAY OUT THIS WEEK, and yes, this is me being more conservative than your physio. He cleared training and intensity, which I am acting on in full. He did not specifically clear loading a bent knee through 20-40 degrees on a knee with confirmed inflammation, and the honest reason to skip them is simpler: at 17 days out there is no strength adaptation left to bank, so they are all downside. If you want them back, ask him directly next week. SELF-CARE: do not foam-roll the IT band itself, you are compressing a structure whose problem is compression. Roll the TFL at the front of the hip, the glutes, and the outer quad above the knee. No ice on the shockwave site for 48h, icing suppresses exactly the inflammatory response the treatment was trying to provoke. GUT TRAINING CONTINUES: 80 g/h means 2 Enervit Carbo Gel C2:1 Pro per hour with 150-250ml of water per gel. This is a 60-minute session, so one gel at minute 30.
